FOUND BY THIS THREAD, NOT YET A RULE ANYWHERE
- A kept branch cannot be brought in by a merge commit when anything on main conflicts with it: the merge round runs a plain `git rebase` whenever main has moved, which is always, and a rebase discards the merge commit and its resolution. What works, used for SEL-045R round four and SEL-043 round two: in the new worktree, `git reset --hard <kept branch>` then `git rebase <launch tip>`, resolving any conflict in the commit where it occurs. A redrive starts a fresh worktree from main and does not resume the kept branch by itself; without an addendum saying so, the session redoes the work.
- Dispatcher test scenarios shared one test database and the same task names; SEL-043 round two fixed it in `tests/dispatch_scaffold.py` (`register` deletes an earlier same-named task). `test_dispatch_parallel` failed the same way in that round's bisect, so one of Issue d6040ce8's two "load flakes" may have been this cause and not load. Not established.
- The operator's Mac sleeping stalled a running session for an hour (SEL-045R round two, 15:14 to 16:13 EST) and made three scheduled checks blind.

WHAT THIS THREAD GOT WRONG
1. SEL-046 changed a line in `_merge()` without reading the kept branch's diff of that file; SEL-041's branch added a line directly above it. That cost SEL-045R round two (code conflict).
2. ADDENDUM 01 to SEL-045R ordered the conflict resolved in a merge commit, without reading what the merge round does to a merge commit. That cost round three. Only then was the whole path simulated in a scratch clone, which is what should have been done before the first redrive.
3. SEL-043 and SEL-044 were redriven as they stood, per SLD-2's handoff, without stating from the code what tier their merges would gate at. Each ran the full serial suite and held the lease for 81 to 96 minutes while factory waited. SLD-2's handoff item 5 asked for exactly that statement.
